repairs.value: Sincere religious experience may warrant private belief, but sincerity alone proves neither supernatural doctrine nor any authority to impose that doctrine on children or others.
repairs.rationale: This preserves the private-experience distinction, doctrinal nonproof, and anti-imposition inference in a concise complete sentence.

repairs.value: Strongest feature: Hitchens sharply distinguishes sincere experience from independently verified supernatural interpretation and, further, from any entitlement to impose religious doctrine on children or other people. Principal limitation: Although subjective conviction underdetermines metaphysical explanation, the rhetorically loaded virgin-birth illustration offers no adequately discriminating evidential comparison, while labeling belief an illusion partially assumes the conclusion at issue. Live burden: The reply directly answers Sharpton’s personal confirmation without denying its psychological reality, but must still demonstrate why naturalistic alternatives explain the experience better than the strongest theistic interpretation. Locked score: 87 appropriately rewards logical coherence, exceptional responsiveness, motion-level relevance, and disciplined scope, while withholding higher credit because evidential comparison remains thin, loaded rhetoric weakens charity, and corrupted captions constrain illustrative precision.
repairs.rationale: This preserves the locked strength, weakness, live comparative burden, and score while replacing truncated filler with argument-specific evaluation.
